items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: And I went with Huey Swift out there and worked over there three or four years

ctx.x: I got it, I see. And how long were you with Al when? Well I say a little more than a year or something. And how long were you with Irene Wilson, I guess her name was?

Yeah, Irene Wilson. Well we stayed at the bookstore about a couple of years, you know. Couple of years. Yeah. And I went with Huey Swift out there and worked over there three or four years, but the federal people closed that place. I don't know what was wrong, something was wrong there. And they closed it up, let's close it completely up. So that's the time I went with this Francois Louisianans.
Well that's all very confusing to me because there's too many bands. Like, you worked with Tiny Palm some, didn't you?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: He was the first Negro band in Chicago that went on the air.

ctx.x: H&T Tavern, huh? Yeah, that's right. Who did he work with that you know of?

King Oliver, General Morton, and a fella you don't know of. Huey Swift. He was the first Negro band in Chicago that went on the air. First one. He had a beat playing. I was good at him. Jeffery Tavern, the name was Jeffery Tavern, South Chicago and Jeffery. And the car dope, and the place closed it down.
Did you see him with Jelly Roll Morton or did he tell you about it? Oh Cliff?
